verdict.label: Self-serve
verdict.summary: No provider review: register an OAuth app (or a GitHub App, which GitHub prefers) in Developer settings, paste Composio's callback URL, and real users can connect the same day.

composioFit.summary: Composio provides a managed OAuth app for GitHub. Creating your own OAuth app is optional and primarily useful for custom consent branding, custom scopes, or dedicated rate limit quotas.
whyOwnApp: Display your own product branding and name on GitHub's OAuth authorization screen.
Request custom scopes beyond default managed app permissions.
Avoid sharing GitHub REST API rate limits (5,000 requests/hour) with other Composio managed app users.

phases.name: Create Auth Config in Composio
steps: Navigate to Composio Dashboard -> Auth Configs -> Create Auth Config.
Select GitHub as toolkit and OAuth2 as auth scheme.
Copy the generated Redirect URI / Callback URL.
phases.handoff: Copy the Composio Redirect URI to use when registering your application on GitHub.

phases.name: Register GitHub OAuth App
steps: Go to GitHub Settings -> Developer Settings -> OAuth Apps -> Register a new application.
Enter Application Name, Homepage URL, and paste Composio's Redirect URI into Authorization callback URL.
Click Register application, then click Generate a new client secret.
phases.handoff: Copy the generated Client ID and Client Secret.

phases.name: Link Credentials in Composio
steps: Paste Client ID and Client Secret back into your Composio Auth Config.
Save configuration and initiate an account connection test.
phases.handoff: Your custom GitHub OAuth integration is active and ready for users.

artefacts.title: GitHub OAuth App Form Details
artefacts.body:

artefacts.title: GitHub OAuth App Security Checklist
artefacts.body: - Avoid using sensitive or internal URLs in public fields.\n- Verify the callback URL matches your Composio auth config redirect URI.\n- Securely store your Client Secret and never expose it in client-side code.

requirements.label: Privacy Policy URL
requirements.when: Optional when registering a basic GitHub OAuth app

requirements.label: Domain Verification
requirements.when: Not required for GitHub OAuth apps

scopes.purpose: Grants full read and write access to public and private repositories, commits, webhooks, and invitations.
Grants read and write access to user profile info, user email addresses, and user followers.
Requests expiring access tokens (8 hours) and refresh tokens (6 months).

redirectRules.rule: Authorization redirect URI must match the registered callback URL exactly or GitHub returns redirect_uri_mismatch.
You can register up to 10 authorization callback URLs per GitHub OAuth app.

blockers.symptom: Connected via your GitHub App, but repository tools return 404 / 'Resource not accessible by integration'
blockers.cause: The user authorized the GitHub App but never installed it on the account or organization that owns the repositories (permissions come from the installation, not auth-config scopes).
blockers.fix: Send users your GitHub App's installation link (github.com/apps/<your-app>/installations/new) and have them select the repositories, then retry.
blockers.fallback: Use an OAuth app with the repo scope (broader access, no installation step), or Composio's managed GitHub app while prototyping.

blockers.cause: The redirect_uri provided in the authorization request does not match the registered callback URL in GitHub.
blockers.fix: Update your GitHub OAuth app settings to include the exact Composio callback URL.
blockers.fallback: Use Composio managed app while fixing redirect URI parameters.

blockers.cause: The GitHub OAuth app has been suspended due to reported abuse, spam, or API misuse.
blockers.fix: Contact GitHub support or review account security notifications to resolve suspension.
blockers.fallback: Switch back to Composio managed OAuth.

blockers.cause: The user rejected or canceled the authorization request on GitHub.
blockers.fix: Prompt the user to restart the OAuth connection process and grant permissions.
blockers.fallback: Explain required permissions to the user prior to triggering authorization.

blockers.cause: Exceeded REST API primary rate limit (5,000 req/hr for authenticated users) or secondary rate limit.
blockers.fix: Check x-ratelimit-reset header and pause requests until reset time.
blockers.fallback: Consider GitHub Enterprise Cloud organization membership for higher limits (15,000 req/hr).

checklist.text: Determine if Composio Managed OAuth meets your scope and branding needs
Create Auth Config in Composio dashboard and copy callback URL
Open GitHub Developer Settings -> OAuth Apps
Click Register a new application and fill in public details
Paste Composio Redirect URI into Authorization callback URL field
Generate a new Client Secret and record Client ID and Client Secret
Enter Client ID and Client Secret into Composio Auth Config and save
Test OAuth login flow and verify access token generation

claims.text: Composio provides a managed OAuth app for GitHub, making custom app creation optional.
claims.quote: Composio-managed OAuth available? Yes

claims.text: Custom auth configs allow configuring custom branding, scopes, rate limits, or custom instances.
claims.quote: You can still create a custom auth config for branding, scopes, rate limits, polling intervals, or custom instances.

claims.text: A GitHub user or organization account can register up to 100 OAuth apps.
claims.quote: A user or organization can own up to 100 OAuth apps.

claims.text: GitHub allows registering up to 10 callback URLs per OAuth app.
claims.quote: You can enter up to 10 callback URLs. To add additional callback URLs, click Add callback URL .

claims.text: When expiring access tokens are enabled, access tokens expire after eight hours and refresh tokens expire after six months without use.
claims.quote: The access token expires after eight hours, and the refresh token expires after six months without use.

claims.text: Requesting the offline_access scope returns an expiring access token and refresh token even if the app is not globally configured to expire tokens.
claims.quote: Requests an expiring access token and a refresh token, even if your OAuth app is not configured to use expiring tokens.

claims.text: Temporary authorization codes issued by GitHub expire after 10 minutes.
claims.quote: The temporary code will expire after 10 minutes.

claims.text: GitHub does not expose an OpenID Connect discovery document at standard well-known endpoints.
GitHub does not expose an OAuth 2.0 authorization server discovery document at standard well-known endpoints.
Primary REST API rate limit for authenticated users is 5,000 requests per hour.
claims.quote: All of these requests count towards your personal rate limit of 5,000 requests per hour.

claims.text: GitHub limits OAuth access token requests to no more than 2,000 per hour.
claims.quote: No more than 2,000 OAuth access token requests per hour are allowed for GitHub Apps and OAuth apps.

claims.text: GitHub returns redirect_uri_mismatch if the redirect_uri in the request does not match the registered callback URL.
claims.quote: If you provide a redirect_uri that doesn't match what you've registered with your application, GitHub will redirect to the registered callback URL with the following parameters summarizing the error:

claims.text: GitHub returns access_denied if the user rejects authorization.
claims.quote: If the user rejects access to your application, GitHub will redirect to the registered callback URL with the following parameters summarizing

claims.text: GitHub redirects with application_suspended if the OAuth app is suspended.
claims.quote: If the OAuth app you set up has been suspended (due to reported abuse, spam, or a mis-use of the API), GitHub will redirect to the registered callback URL using the following parameters to summarize t

claims.text: The repo scope grants full read and write access to public and private repositories.
claims.quote: repo Grants full access to public and private repositories including read and write access to code, commit statuses, repository invitations, collaborators, deployment statuses, and repository webhooks

claims.text: The user scope grants read and write access to profile info, including user:email and user:follow.
claims.quote: user Grants read/write access to profile info only. Note that this scope includes user:email and user:follow .

claims.text: Users can edit requested scopes during authorization and grant less access than requested.
claims.quote: However, users can edit their scopes, effectively granting your application less access than you originally requested.

claims.text: GitHub OAuth apps do not require a mandatory provider review or approval queue prior to production usage.
claims.reason: GitHub documentation for OAuth apps does not describe an application submission or review process for basic production usage.

claims.text: Registering a custom auth config in Composio requires entering the Client ID and Client Secret obtained from the provider.
claims.quote: For OAuth toolkits, register an app in the provider's developer portal and add the redirect URI from the dashboard. Then copy the Client ID and Client Secret back into Composio.

claims.text: GitHub generally prefers GitHub Apps over OAuth apps; both use OAuth 2.0, but OAuth apps can only act on behalf of a user.
claims.quote: In general, GitHub Apps are preferred over OAuth apps. Both OAuth apps and GitHub Apps use OAuth 2.0.

claims.text: GitHub Apps use fine-grained permissions instead of the broad scopes OAuth apps use (e.g. reading code with an OAuth app needs the full repo scope).
claims.quote: GitHub Apps use fine-grained permissions. For example, if your app needs to read the contents of a repository, an OAuth app would require the repo scope

claims.text: Everything in the OAuth app registration is treated as public; GitHub warns against internal URLs or sensitive data.
claims.quote: Only use information in your OAuth app that you consider public. Avoid using sensitive data, such as internal URLs, when creating an OAuth app.

claims.text: Composio accepts your own GitHub App (client ID and secret in the GitHub auth config), not only an OAuth app.
claims.quote: You can bring your own GitHub App by configuring its client ID and client secret in the GitHub auth config.

claims.text: With a GitHub App, each user must still install the app and grant repository access; Composio does not yet send the installation link automatically.
claims.quote: Composio does not currently provide the GitHub App installation link automatically during this flow.

claims.text: Composio manages an OAuth app for GitHub: toolkits.get("github") returns composioManagedAuthSchemes [OAUTH2].

uncertainties: Whether self-hosted GitHub Enterprise Server instances support expiring tokens or offline_access scope in your target environment.
